title: Possible county purchase of Maui Land and Pine water assets
summary: On Aug. 19, the committee voted 7–0 to meet privately on buying an irrigation company's water assets, after the chair deferred the item. The chair said this covers the non-potable side, since the potable side was already voted on.

boards.name: Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Item on the proposed acquisition of the irrigation company's water infrastructure assets: The chair deferred the item because the committee had to leave the room.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The vote to go into executive session was seven ayes and zero noes.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Motion to enter executive session on DRIP 9.12, the proposed acquisition of an irrigation company's water infrastructure assets: The motion passed 7–0, with two members excused.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said this purchase covers the non-potable side, since the committee already voted on the potable side.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the water and land purchase must be discussed privately due to a nondisclosure agreement.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county wants about $2.9 million in improvements to that system after the sale closes.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The system has two stream diversions, two shaft wells, one well, and three reservoirs.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county is proposing to buy a private irrigation company's non-potable (not for drinking) water system.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The item will come back after the administration has and reviews the reports a member requested.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The deputy corporation counsel said the County could try to negotiate conditions on water credits, such as for owner-occupied housing.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: With no objections, the chair deferred the item to bring it back later.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: An official said new water uses will still need a state water use permit after the County buys the assets.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Another member said he supports buying the assets but is concerned about turning farm land into homes.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The administration was asked to tell committee staff once it has reviewed the documents so the item can be put back on an agenda.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A member asked to meet again after the county gets the due diligence documents and preliminary title reports.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A question about eminent domain was set aside for a possible later executive session (a closed-door discussion).
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Water staff said the county would not give water credits to golf courses.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A member said she would like any housing land kept in a land trust for residents.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair confirmed the company wants to keep three parcels and only asks the County to support rezoning.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Water staff said adding water to the upcountry system would help with the water meter waiting list.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said MLP proposes to keep ownership of those parcels.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A member questioned putting homes next to large active pineapple fields.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A member said she wants to make sure the rezoned land does not end up as vacant luxury lots.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said none of the parcels being looked at have active farm operations on them.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said the council would have to approve any final purchase.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said any zoning change would likely be started by the county if it supports the proposals.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Another testifier said Kanaka Maoli need a stronghold in water decisions.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A testifier supported removing private companies from owning public trust water but raised concerns about water credits.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: One testifier said the community wants water put back toward ʻāina and local communities, not private interests.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The administration plans to bring the Council an offer and resolution after reviews and appraisals.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The County also wants land to build a 100 million gallon reservoir.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county will finish due diligence and appraisals before bringing an offer and resolution to the council.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county will do due diligence, title reports and appraisals, then come to the council with an offer and resolution.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county will also consider requests to change zoning on some properties to support housing.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The West Maui assets listed include a ditch system, two tunnels, two reservoirs and four wells.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: On May 18, 2026, the mayor announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU, a written outline of basic terms) with the company.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said these purchases, with others discussed this week, would raise public control of West Maui drinking water systems from about 45% to 93%.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said the goal is long-term water care in the face of climate change, drought and the need for more reliable systems.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county is in early talks to possibly buy Maui Land and Pineapple Company water assets in West Maui and upcountry.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A council member said members are concerned the administration's proposal is incomplete, with no appraisals.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Committee meetings on the purchase are planned for July 27 and July 29.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The water purchase resolution goes to the budget committee, with presentations in committee.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A council member plans to ask the administration about an agreement (MOU) signed May 18, 2026.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Resolution 26-116, acquisition of water system assets: The water system purchase resolution was referred to the Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting
